topic: 情态动词进阶运用：义务、禁止与友好建议 (Modal Verbs: Must, Mustn't, Should, Shouldn't & Can)
teaching_notes: 情态动词就像是动词前面的“情绪调节器”，能帮我们表达规则要求、礼貌建议或行为许可。同学们要牢记两大核心黄金法则：第一，情态动词（must/should/can等）后面必须直接跟动词原形（Base Form），绝对不要加-s、-ed或-ing；第二，注意语气强度的区别——must 表示学校或法律的强制要求（必须），mustn't 表示绝对不可以做的禁止事项（严禁），而 should / shouldn't 则是朋友或老师给出的暖心建议（应该/不应该）。例句 1: You must fasten your seatbelt in the car.（乘车时你必须系好安全带——安全法则）；例句 2: You look exhausted; you should go to bed early tonight.（你看起来很疲惫，今晚应该早点睡——关切建议）。

questions.question: Students ______ run in the school hallways because they might slip and get hurt.
questions.explanation: 走廊奔跑极易滑倒受伤，这是学校明令禁止的行为，因此用表示严厉禁止的情态动词 mustn't（绝不能、严禁）。

questions.question: The science exam is tomorrow morning. You ______ play video games all night.
questions.explanation: 明天早上有科学考试，熬夜打游戏是不明智的行为。此处表示劝告和建议，应用 shouldn't（不应该）。

questions.question: Leo is very talented in music. He ______ play three different instruments smoothly.
questions.explanation: 句意表示 Leo 具备演奏三种乐器的能力，表示“能力”用 can。情态动词无人称变化，不能加 -s，故 D 错误。

questions.question: Every passenger ______ wear a seatbelt before the flight takes off.
questions.explanation: 起飞前系好安全带是航空硬性安全规定，应用 must（必须）。情态动词后直接接动词原形，不能加 to，排除 D。

questions.question: Excuse me, Mr. Green. ______ I borrow a blue marker from your desk?
questions.explanation: 在向老师提出礼貌请求或许可时，常用 May I... ?（我可以……吗？）。

questions.question: You look very pale and have a high fever. You ______ see the school nurse immediately.
questions.explanation: 同学脸色苍白且发烧，提出合理的就医建议应用 should（应该）。情态动词后直接接动词原形 see，不加 to。

questions.question: In the library, all visitors ______ keep quiet so others can read peacefully.
questions.explanation: 在图书馆保持安静是基本公共规则，用 must 表示“必须遵守”。

questions.question: Look at the sign! It says: 'Danger! You ______ swim in this deep river.'
questions.explanation: 标牌明确警示有危险，严禁在此深河游泳，表示禁止用 mustn't。

questions.question: My little sister ______ tie her own shoelaces when she was only four years old.
questions.explanation: 由时间状语 when she was only four years old 可知描述过去具备的能力，can 的过去式是 could。

questions.question: You ______ brush your teeth twice a day to keep your gums healthy.
questions.explanation: 每天刷牙两次以保持牙龈健康属于卫生保健的好建议，用 should（应该）。ought 后必须搭配 to，因此 D 不完整。

questions.question: The museum guide warned us that we ______ touch the ancient glass vases.
questions.explanation: 博物馆向导警告严禁触摸古代玻璃花瓶，表示禁止用 mustn't。

questions.question: Emma has finished all her chores, so she ______ go outside and ride her bicycle now.
questions.explanation: 做完了家务，得到了去室外骑自行车的许可/可能，用 can（可以）。

questions.question: To protect our environment, we ______ waste clean water or leave the tap running.
questions.explanation: 为了保护环境，我们不应该浪费洁净水或任由水龙头流淌，shouldn't 表示“不应该”。

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically CORRECT?

options.A: She must wears a uniform on Mondays.
options.B: She must to wear a uniform on Mondays.
options.C: She must wear a uniform on Mondays.
options.D: She must wearing a uniform on Mondays.

questions.explanation: 情态动词 must 后面必须紧接动词原形 wear，不能加三单-s、to 或 -ing，因此 C 选项完全正确。

questions.question: It's starting to rain heavily. You ______ take an umbrella with you before heading out.
questions.explanation: 外面下大雨，建议出门前带上伞，用 should 表达合理建议。

questions.question: You ______ feed the monkeys at the zoo; it is strictly against the zoo regulations.
questions.explanation: 后半句提到 strictly against the zoo regulations（严格违反动物园规定），说明这是严令禁止的行为，选 mustn't。

questions.question: ______ you please pass me the salt shaker, Lucas?
questions.explanation: Could you please...? 是英语中极其常用且礼貌的请求句型，意为“你能否请帮我……？”。

questions.question: Sam felt sick after eating five cupcakes. He ______ eat so much junk food in one go.
questions.explanation: 吃了五个纸杯蛋糕后身体不适，说明一次性吃这么多垃圾食品是不可取的，用 shouldn't 表达事理建议。

questions.question: Pedestrians ______ look both ways carefully before they step off the curb.
questions.explanation: 过马路前行人必须仔细观察马路两边，关乎生命安全的硬性规则用 must。

questions.question: Lucas didn't practice the piano this week, so he ______ play the sonata accurately during today's lesson.
questions.explanation: 因为本周没有练习，所以在今天的课上“无法/不能”准确弹奏奏鸣曲，表示当下能力无法做到用 can't (cannot)。
